merged.author: Lynder063
merged.untrustedBody:
Working PR for level 18 (Veldin 2, `src/overlays/l18_veldin2/`). Everything we get goes in here, matched or not; still a draft.

## Status

Level 18: **79 of 122 functions exact, 29,360 of 154,848 bytes** (19.0% of the level's code, **26.5%** counting the staged near misses). 42 were already matched before this branch. Two more are matched but invisible to the report, which does not see a definition whose name is an `__asm__` alias (`func_L18_002D6B58`, `func_L18_002F1AB0`); those drop out of the totals instead of counting, which is why the function count fell from 123.

Plus `func_L05_003053D8` (level 5), which the tooling fix below unblocked.

Every function is checked with `tools/try_func.py` (every byte and relocation at its real level address), re-checked in the final file with `tools/overlay_file_check.py`, and `progress/report.json` is regenerated in the same commit.

merged.title: fix(nonmatching): level 18: func_L18_002D93C0 from a size mismatch to…
merged.author: Lynder063
merged.untrustedBody:
… 20 bytes

Two things: the byte at entry+0x74 is read unsigned in retail (`lbu`), which needs the D_0013E633 blob declared `unsigned char` through an alias because the file declares it `char`; and the four paths share one store of the result instead of storing per branch. What is left is retail re-materialising `addiu $v0,$zero,-1` on each path against our one register.

opened.title: Level 18: func_L18_002D7310 to size exact (77.9% fuzzy)
opened.author: Lynder063
opened.untrustedBody:
## Summary

- `func_L18_002D7310` (level 18, 484 bytes) goes from a size mismatch (488) to size-exact with 107 bytes off, so its fuzzy score in the report goes from 0 % to 77.9 %. It is staged in `nonmatching/`, not landed.
- What got it there:
  - The post-call code is written in both branches, so gcc crossjumps the two calls into retail's single shared `jal`.
  - Prototype B for `func_L00_0025F4A8` fixes the argument order. Exact callers in l13, l17 and shared already use it: 108 bytes off against 124 (A) and 137 (C).
  - `((unsigned char *)moby)[0xA4] = 0xFF`. Through a `char *`, gcc turns 0xFF into -1 and shares it with the later `-1` stack argument.
- What is left: the scheduling order of the argument setup, and which of `$2`/`$3` the shared tail uses.

- `func_L18_002D9C78`/`002D9C90`, `002D9440`/`002D9460`, `002E0F90`, `002F1420`/`002F1444`: each is one real function that the catalogue split into two. The first half branches into the second. C

The level overlays' dispatch tables are keyed by **class identifier**, and those identifiers are stable between the prototype builds and the retail. That axis had not been measured: the 2026-10-01 pass tested *position* (same index in both tables) and closed the lead on that basis.

merged.author: llesieur99

Adds `docs/ENGINE-SYMBOL-NAMES.md`.

The CreepNT prototype-research repository binds eleven engine symbols to fixed addresses
in a linker script (`patches/cust_main_menu_src/frontend.ld`) so that a replacement main
menu can be linked against the 8 August 2003 prototype. Those addresses had never been
tested against the retail image.

one at a time, on what the code at its address must do:

| Symbol | Retail boot at that address | Verdict |

| `FlushCache` `0x0011aea0` | first of three consecutive SDK cache syscall stubs (number 100) | **transfers** |
| `sprintf` `0x00115da0` | last two instructions of a function starting at `0x00115d48` | no |
| `PAD` `0x00138080` | a 32-byte block display setup sends to the IPU by DMA (channel 4, QWC=4) | no |
| `Settings` `0x00139e18` | zeros, referenced nowhere | unproven - not named |

merged.title: Name 102 assert-message carriers, and close the last 59 messages
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
Adds `docs/ASSERT-MESSAGE-NAMES.md` and `docs/assert-message-names.tsv`.

After the dispatch-table pass, **59 assert messages** localized in the retail boot still had
no carrying function: no instruction computes their address, in the retail boot or in the
prototype boot. This closes that family.

**Method.** The prototype's level archives were extracted with our own ISO9660 reader and
section reader — 27 levels, 57 070 528 bytes. The level table sits at
`RC2.HDR + 0x5000 + i*0x3000` (not at the offset an earlier note assumed); that was verified
against the volume's real LBAs. 32 of the 59 messages occur inside the retail level overlays,
and their carriers were resolved by reference.

**Result: 102 functions named across 25 overlays.**

| Name | Functions |
| --- | ---: |
| `DirectionalLightsOverflow` | 25 |
| `CameraCollPrimTestGridOutOfBounds` | 25 |
| `LevelDoorLimitExceeded` | 25 |
| `NpcShowMessageBadId` | 10 |
| `PathSetWtoDistNullPath` | 7 |
| `ThermanatorBallsNeededReport` | 5

merged.title: Identify which prototype the linker script maps: the 6 August 2003 preview disc
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
Adds an update section to `docs/ENGINE-SYMBOL-NAMES.md`: which prototype the linker script
actually maps.

`patches/_iso_patch.toml` declares where it patches — a boot ELF at file offset `0x229800`,
size `1541852`. The **6 August 2003 preview disc** places its boot (`SCUS_972.68`,
1 541 852 bytes) at **LBA 1107**, exactly that offset, and all three patch sites the file
documents are **byte-identical** there:

| Patch site | What the patch file says it replaces | 6 August boot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0x0021d0b8` | a store, a return and a stack adjustment | identical |
| `0x001fc7d4` | a call to `movie()` and its delay-slot load | identical |
| `0x001fc95c` | the colour build for the "Alpha/Preview Disk" text | identical |

So `frontend.ld` maps the **6 August** image — the repository's "aug8" name is not what it
indexes. The 8 August disc could not be tested (its download returns 404).

This also settles what the earlier failure meant. On that build the names are right, and
checkable o

merged.title: Add a measured survey of the prototype builds: the earliest one is the closest to retail
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
Adds `docs/PROTOTYPE-BUILDS.md`: a measured survey of the three 2003 prototype builds we
hold, and what each is good for.

**None of them carries symbols.** All three boots have zero `.symtab` / `.mdebug`
sections — the shortcut that gave an authentic `MobyInstance` on a Deadlocked prototype
does not exist for Going Commando on any disc we hold.

**The 7 and 9 September discs are the same code**: identical section tables (same entry
point, same `core.*` sizes, same 52 `.DVP.overlay.*` sections), and exactly the same
comparison numbers against the retail. They differ by 8 192 bytes of data.

**The useful result inverts the natural assumption — the earliest build is the closest:**

| Identical bytes vs retail | `core.text` | `core.data` | `core.rdata` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 6 August 2003 | **26.5 %** | **93.8 %** | **88.7 %** |
| 7 September 2003 | 12.1 % | 91.4 % | 22.4 % |

The September builds add ~11 400 bytes to `core.text`, which shifts everything after it.

merged.title: Document the level archive format, measured rather than inherited
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
Adds `docs/LEVEL-ARCHIVE-FORMAT.md`: how this engine family stores its levels, as read with
our own readers and **verified against the volume's real LBAs** — not inherited from an
existing note.

**What it documents**

- the volume (ISO9660, boot and `RC2.HDR` locations, one `LEVEL`/`SCENE` archive pair per level);
- the level table — `RC2.HDR + 0x5000 + i*0x3000`, level LBA at `+0x0004`, scene LBA at
  `+0x1804`, checked against the real ISO9660 LBAs for levels 0–5. An existing community
  note places it at `+0x4888` with a 24-byte stride; **that layout does not hold on these
  discs**;
- the archive itself: a header whose data offset is **found by validation rather than
  assumed**, a 12-byte-range header, then a chained list of
  `(destination, size, type, entry point)` records followed by their content — seven
  sections per level (`.lit`, `.bss`, `.data`, `lvl.vtbl`, `lvl.camvtbl`, `lvl.sndvtbl`,
  `.text`), 27 levels, **57 070 528 bytes**;
- **the same reader parses the 6 August
